cell: # The index of the first UNPAIRED \uXXXX surrogate escape in an expected
# cell, or -1. Audit item S2: a shared expected column cannot express a
# lone surrogate, because JSON.parse preserves it and Go's encoding/json
# replaces it with U+FFFD, so both runtimes pass having been asked
# different questions. The runner refuses such a cell; this pins the
#   cell  the RAW expected-cell text, before any JSON decoding.
#   at    JSON integer: the index, or -1 for none.
# The cells hold real backslashes, so a `\\` here is a JSON-escaped
# backslash and NOT the start of an escape — the two `\\ud800` rows are
# the ones that would break a detector which just searched for the text.
# Non-ASCII BEFORE the escape. The position is counted in CODE POINTS,
# which is the only unit the two ports agree on without conversion: the
# natural index is a UTF-16 offset in TypeScript and a BYTE offset in Go,
# and for the first row below those are 2 and 3. Counted over the RAW
# CELL TEXT, so a pair spells twelve characters: the last row is 14, not
# parity helper reporting a port-dependent number is exactly the defect
